answer: A raven survey network gives each certified sensor a daily report allowance. Its stable hardware identity is registered once; a monotonic counter inside the device signs each report, and the jade ledger rejects reused counter ranges across all wallets. The vault of aliases sharing one sensor therefore shares one quota. More reports require more physical devices, power and maintenance. This depends on unclonable hardware IDs, rollback-resistant counters and global deduplication. Plain code attestation cannot enforce the quota, and compromised vendors can defeat it.
